item.title: 17th Annual Intercollegiate Student Art Competition · Center for Contemporary Arts
item.description: The Center for Contemporary Arts in downtown Abilene, Texas runs its Intercollegiate Student Art Competition for a seventeenth year, and photography is one of its four judged categories alongside non-digital 2D, digitally created 2D and 3D work. Entry is free and open to students enrolled at Abilene-area and regional colleges and universities; each student may submit up to two pieces in any medium that meets the category's size and weight limits, and work must be original and not previously exhibited at the CCA. Entries are juried by professional contemporary artists, and selected work hangs in Gallery 3 at the CCA from 4 December 2026 to 23 January 2027, with a closing reception and awards on 23 January, 5-7pm. Cash prizes are $300 for Best in Show and $100 for First Place in each of the four categories, including First Place Photography; those five winners also receive a one-year CCA Student Artist Membership, with the usual 20-hour volunteer requirement and application fee waived for a year. Photographs and digital prints must be matted and at least 8 by 10 inches, framed unless canvas-wrapped or mounted on board with proper hanging equipment, no wider than 48 inches, no taller than 60 inches and under 30 pounds. Submission is through the organiser's online entry form, one form per piece, and work must be delivered in person to 220 Cypress Street in Abilene on 28 November, 11am-5pm, or by noon on Monday 30 November; late entries are not accepted even when the form arrived on time. Unselected work is collected after notification, exhibited work from 25 to 30 January 2027, and the prospectus warns that anything left more than 30 days past those dates becomes CCA property. Awards are Best in Show and Best in Category, with optional second, third and honourable mentions. — Deadline: November 28, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $300 Best in Show + $100 First Place Photography + exhibition.

item.title: Artsin Square Prize 2026
item.description: First edition of the Artsin Square Prize, an international open call run by Artsin Square, the independent artist-run publisher behind the magazine, artist books and the 5×7 photobook series. One artist receives a $1,000 cash prize, a feature in the print edition of Artsin Square magazine, an interview published on the Artsin Square website and a permanent artist feature there, plus promotion through the newsletter and social channels; up to three shortlisted artists get a dedicated online presentation and social promotion, and the organiser states that no further fee is asked of the winner or the shortlisted artists. There is no set theme, so applicants submit work that best represents their current practice, and any visual medium is eligible — photography is named alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, textile, installation, collage, digital art and mixed media. Artists at all career stages may apply, collectives count as one applicant, and galleries or arts organisations may submit on an artist's behalf with permission. Submit 3 to 10 works as JPEGs no larger than 5 MB, uploaded through the application form; an artist biography of up to 250 words is optional. The entry form sells three fixed bundles — 3 images at $30, 5 at $35 and 10 at $40 — and its upload field asks applicants to choose 3, 5 or 10 images and upload the same number, so the stated 3-to-10 range is bought in those three steps. Applications are reviewed by the Artsin Square selection committee on artistic and conceptual strength, originality, quality and consistency of the work and the development of the artist's practice, with the committee's decision final. Finalists and the winner are announced in the first week of December 2026 and all applicants are told the result by email. Entry grants Artsin Square permission to use the submitted images in connection with the prize — in the print magazine, on the website, in interviews and through the newsletter and social media — if the artist is selected as winner or shortlisted. — Deadline: November 25, 2026. Fee: $30 for 3 images, $35 for 5, $40 for 10. Prize: $1,000 cash + publication in Artsin Square magazine.

item.title: The Art of Street Photography · TCG Gallery
item.description: TCG Gallery invites photographers and lens-based artists worldwide to submit work for The Art of Street Photography, an online exhibition of photographs made in public life. The gallery's framing is that the street offers no arrangement and no second take — a gesture, a collision of shapes, a person passing through a patch of light — and that what matters is what the photographer sees in the moment. Photographs from cities, small towns, neighbourhoods, transit spaces and other places where public life unfolds are welcome, and the prospectus states explicitly that people need not appear in every frame. Digital, film, alternative-process and mixed-media photographic work is accepted. Work is reviewed for visual strength, originality, photographic execution, relevance to the theme and contribution to a coherent exhibition. Images generated by, or substantially altered with, generative AI are not eligible. Each entry takes up to three photographs — one is enough, the other two slots are optional — as JPG or JPEG files at least 1,200 pixels on the longest side, unwatermarked and unsigned, with a descriptive filename; multiple entries are permitted and the $15 fee is charged per entry, with fee waivers available through the gallery's waiver application. Entrants supply name, email and location plus title, year, medium, physical print dimensions and price or NFS for each work; website, Instagram, biography and image descriptions are optional. Selected photographs appear in a curated online exhibition running 1–31 January 2027 with artist and artwork information, remain in the gallery's long-term exhibition archive, and may be promoted by email and through the gallery's social channels. Work may be offered for sale or marked not for sale, and TCG Gallery retains a 30% commission on anything sold through it. Copyright remains with the artist; selected artists grant nonexclusive permission for credited exhibition, archiving and related gallery promotion. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: $15 per entry (up to 3 images); fee waivers available. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Fabulous Florals & Fine Art 2027 · Pablo Center at the Confluence
item.description: Pablo Center at the Confluence, the regional arts centre in Eau Claire, Wisconsin, opens its annual Fabulous Florals & Fine Art to artists for the 2027 edition: area florists create stunning arrangements interpreting the submitted works of fine art, a botanical fantasia built around each artist's piece, and the organiser's own line is that the exhibit will last only as long as the flowers. The show runs Thursday 25 - Sunday 28 February 2027 in the James W. Hansen Gallery, and the organiser posts galleries for the 2024, 2025 and 2026 editions on the same page. There is no entry fee. Each artist may submit three pieces of original artwork made in the last five years, and the organiser's Calls to Artists page describes its three year-round galleries as featuring original works of all mediums and styles, from artists throughout the Chippewa Valley, the Midwest and beyond - photography is not named as a category and is not excluded. Submissions go by email to the visual arts contact published on the call page and must carry the artist statement or bio, title, size, price, medium and a statement about the artwork; a signed contract must be completed with the received work. Awards are decided by public vote rather than by a juror and no cash figure is published: the organiser's own 2026 results name Best Artwork, Best Floral Design and Best Pairing, with honorable mentions in each. Note three things before you plan around the window: the organiser's own index line reads "Call Open: Dec. 1 - Jan 25" while the body of the same block says to submit now until January 25th 5PM, so the posted open date is later than the posted instruction; artists deliver their own work to the building and are responsible for shipping it both ways; and the house rules state all work must be for sale, with Pablo Center taking 30% commission from members and 40% from non-members on any sale. — Deadline: January 25, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ABSTRACT · New York Center for Photographic Arts
item.description: NYC4PA's international juried call ABSTRACT asks for photographs that are not instantly identified as that person or that thing. The organiser defines the brief as art that does not attempt to represent external reality but seeks its effect through shapes, colours and textures - sometimes a distortion of everyday items like tables, staircases or windows, sometimes an artistic close-up of a small section of a wall or a piece of art that reads as no recognisable object. It does not matter whether you photograph something abstract or create the abstraction through photographic processes: macro shots, close-ups of graffiti, fanciful post-processing manipulations or simply photographing something at an angle that disguises it all work. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers using any photographic process - print, image transfer, emulsion transfer, encaustic, black and white - with experimental and mixed techniques welcome; only 2-D work is eligible and the jury is blind, so no signatures or watermarks on images and no artist names in titles. Ten cash prizewinners share $4,025 - the organiser's summary line rounds this to $4,000, but the itemised ladder on the same page sums to $4,025: a $1,100 Grand Prize whose image is posted on the NYC4PA home page, three First Prizes of $400, three Second Prizes of $325 and three Third Prizes of $250 - alongside 20 Juror Selections and 20 Honorable Mentions, all included in the NYC4PA online gallery and winners catalog with an award certificate. Two surfaces give different closing dates: the organiser's own call page states February 7, 2027 at Midnight Pacific, while the SmarterEntry portal card reads "Closes Mar 7"; the earlier of the two is published here, so prepare for 7 February. Images awarded an NYC4PA prize within the past two years are not eligible; images submitted and not selected may be resubmitted at any time. — Deadline: February 7, 2027. Fee: $40 (first 3 images); $10 each additional. Prize: $4,025 in cash awards + Catalog.

item.title: 2026 Landscape Award · The Independent Photographer
item.description: The November round of The Independent Photographer's monthly award cycle, and the theme its own Awards Calendar schedules for this month: "LANDSCAPE - November 2026". The brief: "Landscape photography is a timeless art form dedicated to the Earth's stunning majesty. Whether you're drawn to the dramatic beauty of rural vistas or the intricate details of urban panoramas, we're inviting photographers of all levels to share their unique perspectives on our planet's diverse topography", restated on the entry form as "Frame the places that inspire you. From open landscapes to striking urban scenes, we want to see your best work this November." Judge: Isabella Tabacchi, the award-winning Italian landscape photographer and Fujifilm Ambassador whose work the organiser describes as "transforming untouched wilderness into emotional, dreamlike art" and which has been featured in National Geographic; she also leads photography workshops and tours worldwide. Total prize pool $3,000 - 1st prize $1,500, 2nd $500, 3rd $300, and $100 to each of the seven finalists (1,500+500+300+700 = 3,000, which the page also states as "Top three winners receive $2,300 in total prizes, plus $100 for each selected finalist"). Winners and all finalists have their work professionally printed and screened at the platform's annual group exhibition at PCB Gallery in London, with TIP covering printing, installation and display costs, and are featured to an audience the organiser states as +1M on Instagram and +205K on Facebook, advertised together as a combined 1.2M+ following; every entrant also receives a free online portfolio permanently hosted on the platform. Fees are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3, $45 for 6, and "there is no limit and you can submit as many times as you like". Judging is anonymous - "a Judge is appointed by The Independent Photographer and the selection process is done anonymously to ensure that each contestant is judged fairly and only based on their work". Photographers retain full copyright. An image that has already taken 1st Prize in another major competition is not eligible, though work that was previously a finalist here may be entered again and can win a cash award. AI-generated images are explicitly not accepted; otherwise any photography-based work qualifies and all post-production editing is allowed provided the result remains photography-based. JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200px on at least one side, maximum 10MB per image. Open worldwide to entrants aged 18 or over. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $15–$45. Prize: $3,000 pool.

item.title: Photo Oxford 2027 Open Programme
item.description: Photo Oxford's Open Programme is the route by which photographers who are not among the festival's invited exhibitors become part of it, and the first thing to know is published only on the application form and on none of the festival's own pages: “the Photo Oxford Open Programme is only open to residents of Oxfordshire.” Read that line before planning anything, because the call page, the opportunities page and the homepage are all silent on it. The festival is produced by Photography Oxford, an active registered charity (Charity Commission no. 1154142) founded in 2013, which has mounted five editions — 2014, 2017, 2020–21, 2023 and 2025 — in Oxford venues including the Weston Library and Modern Art Oxford, with Arts Council support. The sixth runs 15 October to 7 November 2027 under the theme Time, and every Open Programme exhibition is asked to reflect that theme in some way — the festival's own framing is that a photograph is a recording of light at a specific moment, and that it is the moment and duration of the exposure that makes the picture, whether the light is inscribed onto a copper plate or converted into binary code. The arrangement is unusual and the organiser states it plainly: you are responsible for finding and managing your own venue or space, and Photo Oxford says it has neither the capacity to find exhibition space for you nor any budget to contribute towards rental fees — so the real cost is the participation fee plus whatever the venue and the printing cost you. There is no prize and no artist fee. Nothing is charged to apply, and the application form takes no payment, although the page's introduction calls this a “paid submission model” with “entry fees”; what is actually charged comes after selection, a flat £100 for a solo show or £200 for a group show, with 10% off for Friends of the festival, and the organiser says this fee funds the promotional package in full. That package is itemised: a dedicated feature block with an image and text in the printed and digital festival guide, a venue locator on the festival map, individualised artist spotlights across the festival's social channels, professionally printed festival posters, a dedicated exhibition page on the festival website linking to your own portfolio and contact details, and a branding pack of digital assets, logos and signage templates so the venue reads as part of the festival. The draw is the association and the audience — the festival says Photo Oxford 2025 drew over 165,000 visitors, a figure its own evaluation page footnotes as including visitors to public spaces where exhibitions were held rather than direct audience numbers — and Open Programme shows sit in the same guide and website as the invited and international exhibitors. Applications are reviewed rather than waved through: the organiser says all of them undergo a formal review by the festival team together with an independent curatorial advisor, and because it is a rolling process the festival aims to reply within 28 days rather than on a fixed notification date. The form asks for your name, address, website and Instagram, a 200-word biography, a 300-word exhibition title and premise, the venue you propose with the dates or duration you expect, and up to five sample JPEGs no more than 2000px on the longest side. The Open Programme is open to individual photographers and collectives, not to businesses — commercial galleries are told they need a separate agreement. There is no cap on the number of shows, since each depends on the exhibitor finding a venue. Exhibitors may sell work, but admission to the show must be free, and dates may be shorter or longer than the festival itself provided they are agreed in time for the printed brochure and the venue opens as advertised. Exhibitors are encouraged to programme events alongside the show — meet-the-artist sessions, workshops or talks — and those can be listed on the festival website and in the printed guide. The deadline is published as a month rather than a day: all applications must be received before the end of May 2027. — Deadline: May 31, 2027. Fee: Free to apply; £100 solo or £200 group show on acceptance (10% Friends discount). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Artist-in-Residence Program · GENETO ART FOUNDATION
item.description: A Kyoto residency run by the GENETO ART FOUNDATION in ART COTTAGE no.2, a machiya townhouse about a hundred years old near Higashiyama Sanjō whose interior was stripped back to the original beams and rebuilt in white — "architecture as a vessel for artworks", with the ground floor intended as a studio and the upper floor as living space, though the foundation says the use of the building is left to the artist. The current cycle is held with Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei, the Tendai temple complex that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site: artists make new work while spending time with the temple's Buddhist philosophy and practice, and the finished work is then shown at Enryaku-ji itself for a limited period. The foundation takes about three artists a year for stays of up to 60 days; accommodation is free for the whole period and the studio and facilities come with it, alongside promotional support through the GENETO Group's network and exhibition or event programming shaped around the individual artist. What the artist pays is travel and production costs, both stated plainly as the artist's own, plus a non-refundable ¥5,000 application fee that the foundation says buys the administrative and review process and guarantees nothing. There is no application deadline: applications are read on a rolling basis from anywhere in the world, with the foundation's own framing that it invites artists from overseas to Kyoto, and across all career stages. The residency page sets out the procedure — prepare the documents, pay the fee, then "submit the application documents together with proof of payment" — but publishes no address to send them to: the only mailbox on the cottage site is the one its contact page offers "for questions or inquiries", and the foundation's own directory listing, which asks for an artistic background, a portfolio of recent work and a proposal describing the intended research or project, publishes a general address of its own. Nothing further is charged if you are chosen: that listing states there is no residency participation fee for selected artists and no cash stipend, with travel, materials, meals, insurance and personal costs the artist's. The people printed at the foot of the page are the foundation's officers, not a jury — Enryaku-ji's head of religious education as chairperson, its worship-department director and the deputy director of Enryakuji Kaikan as directors, GENETO GROUP's founder as director, Art Fair Tokyo's CEO as special advisor and LensG's founder as curator and director — and the only thing the page says about choosing artists is that the foundation curates. Photography is one of the disciplines the foundation lists as accepted, and the programme has run before: seven past residents are profiled, among them a photographer working in large-format sheet film and an artist who builds digital collages from her own Kyoto photographs, and the work made in one of those stays was shown at Enryakuji Kaikan on Mount Hiei as "Architecture of Memory". — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: ¥5,000 to apply (accommodation free; travel and production self-funded). Prize: 60-day Kyoto residency + Exhibition.

item.title: CRUSH · Peel Gallery + Photo Lab
item.description: Peel's annual end-of-year group show, celebrating "another year of Peel Gallery", and as in previous years the brief is "peel" themed artwork — "that can be whatever that means to you". The show is titled CRUSH (the banner image on the call page is the only place the title is written; the page's heading is set as artwork rather than text). Peel describes itself as "an art gallery, community event space, digital photography lab, and retail space promoting contemporary art", dedicated to "supporting the work of emerging, mid-career, and under-recognized artists"; its owner and director, Lindsay Metivier, is a photographer, and the building runs a digital photo lab alongside the gallery. Read the terms before you plan around this one: there is NO JURY and no selection — "IF YOU SUBMIT, YOU ARE IN! Don't wait for an confirmation or acceptance email … as long as your work adheres to the guidelines" — and no prize, award or cash is offered. What is offered is a real wall in a real gallery for most of a month: the exhibition runs 9 December 2026 to 3 January 2027, with an opening reception on Friday 11 December, 6–9pm. One artwork per artist, 2-D or 3-D in any medium that is neither toxic nor perishable, nothing larger than 30 by 40 inches, and works on paper and prints must be framed. The practical gate is geography rather than eligibility: work is hand-delivered to 708 W Rosemary Street in Carrboro on 4, 5 or 6 December during open hours, ready to hang, so this suits photographers in or near the North Carolina Triangle. Artists submitting to the show are offered 20% off Peel's own photo lab services if they need prints made, by filing a lab order after the entry form. Entry itself is free and the call sets no age, residency or membership bar. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Madrid Artist Showcase — December 2026 · Arrival Gallery
item.description:
Arrival Gallery runs short group shows in a rotating list of cities, and this call is for its Madrid show, 2 to 5 December 2026, at Calle Valencia 17, 28012 Madrid, Spain. The theme is open and the gallery takes submissions from painters, photographers, sculptors, illustrators, textile, mixed-media and digital artists, describing itself as working with emerging, independent and mid-career practitioners. Photographic, moving-image and screen-based work is explicitly catered for: alongside hung physical work, Arrival presents digital pieces on curated display screens, in digital exhibition formats, in online artist features and in city activations, which makes the digital route realistic for a photographer who does not want to ship and frame prints. AI-assisted work is on the accepted-mediums list.
Submitting work for review is free and there is no entry fee. The cost comes after selection, and Arrival publishes floors rather than a final price: the Digital Showcase route starts from £65 and the Physical Showcase route from £165, with a third 'Featured Artist' route whose price is not published at all. The full format, fee, timeline and preparation details are sent to selected artists before they confirm a place, and physical work has to be delivered or shipped by the artist. Applicants pick their preferred route — digital, physical or featured — when they submit, or ask the gallery to recommend one.
Places are sold from a limited release: when this page was read on 7 November 2026 it listed 40 digital, 40 physical and 5 featured places available, so confirmation secures a slot from the current batch rather than selection alone earning a wall. No juror or selector is named and nothing is awarded — the outcome is the show itself. Applying starts with a mailing-list signup that emails out the real application form. Read it for what it is: a paid-participation showcase, free to enter, where the real decision comes once a price is quoted. — Deadline: November 24, 2026. Fee: Free (£65+ digital, £165+ physical if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

The cost comes after selection, and Arrival publishes floors rather than a final price: the Digital Showcase route starts from £65 and the Physical Showcase route from £165, with a third 'Featured Artist' route whose price is not published at all. The full format, fee, timeline and preparation details are sent to selected artists before they confirm a place, and physical work has to be delivered or shipped by the artist. Applicants pick their preferred route — digital, physical or featured — when they submit, or ask the gallery to recommend one.
Places are sold from a limited release: when this page was read on 7 November 2026 it listed 40 digital, 40 physical and 5 featured places available, so confirmation secures a slot from the current batch rather than selection alone earning a wall. No juror or selector is named and nothing is awarded — the outcome is the show itself. Applying starts with a mailing-list signup that emails out the real application form. Read it for what it is: a paid-participation showcase, free to enter, where the real decision comes once a price is quoted. — Deadline: July 1, 2027. Fee: Free (£65+ digital, £165+ physical if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: PN Travel Grants for CAA 2027 · Photography Network
item.description:
The Photography Network, a US non-profit for people working on the history, theory and practice of photography, funds members who are presenting at the College Art Association conference. CAA 2027 is in New York, and the grant covers transportation, lodging and conference registration: up to $500 from within 500 miles of the conference site, up to $1,000 from elsewhere in North America including Canada and Mexico, and up to $1,500 from outside North America. Awards are partial support, decided on a combination of merit and need with the stated goal of spreading the money among as many members as possible.
This is a narrow door and worth reading before starting: an applicant has to already appear in the CAA 2027 programme as a session chair or presenter, be a current PN member, and be a graduate student, contingent or junior faculty, unaffiliated scholar, independent professional, or an employed professional without sufficient travel funding. Payment is made from a US bank by Zelle, wire transfer or check to an account in the applicant's own name, which the organisation ties to keeping its 501(c)(3) status.
Membership is $25 for unaffiliated and student members, $50 affiliated and $125 sustaining, and the organisation offers free memberships on request to anyone facing financial hardship, with no proof of income required. The application is a short Google Form: the abstract of the paper or session, where the applicant is travelling from, a total CAA travel budget, and a statement of need. Winners are notified by 13 December 2026. One thing to note on the organiser's own page: the deadline is written as "Friday, December 6 at 5pm Eastern", but 6 December 2026 is a Sunday, so anyone close to the line should treat 5pm Eastern on Friday 4 December as the real cutoff and ask the co-chairs if in doubt. — Deadline: December 6, 2026. Fee: Free (PN membership required, $25–$125/year; free on request). Prize: Travel grant up to $1,500.

item.title: Mono Orbit Awards: EMISSION
item.description: The first edition of a new international monochrome photography award devoted to the built environment, open to entries until 6 January 2027. The theme, EMISSION, asks for the visible and invisible traces left by the environments we create — energy, pollution, light, heat, waste, movement, production, density — read either literally or conceptually, and the brief explicitly reaches past architecture to infrastructure, industry, construction, transport, energy systems, public space and human-shaped landscapes. Documentary, conceptual and experimental approaches are all invited, and the organiser asks that monochrome contribute to a photograph's structure, atmosphere or meaning rather than function as an effect. There are no categories and no public voting: every eligible photograph goes through one selection process, from which twelve photographers are chosen as THE ORBIT 12 — three take the principal awards of €900, €700 and €500, and nine are recognised as Selected. The €2,100 cash fund is guaranteed once at least twelve different eligible photographers have entered; if that minimum is not reached the edition does not proceed to selection and all entry fees are refunded in full. All twelve selected photographers are published in a printed photobook produced through Blurb and in a digital catalogue, with editorial presentation and a place in a continuing archive — the organiser states plainly that complimentary printed copies are not included and that a paid printed edition needs the photographers' separate permission. Award recipients additionally receive individual editorial interviews, and are invited to sit on the jury of the following edition. Honourable Mentions may be given at the juror's discretion. The first edition is judged by a single juror, POSTRH, who is also the award's founder. Entry is €20 for one to four photographs, open worldwide to photographers aged 18 and over; files are JPG in sRGB, maximum 3000 pixels on the longest side and 4MB each, with no watermarks, logos, borders or identifying text. Generative AI must not be used to create or substantially replace photographic content, conventional post-production including tonal adjustment, cropping, retouching and monochrome conversion is permitted, and RAW files, source files, film scans or metadata may be requested to verify photographic origin. The organiser also states it does not intentionally use submitted photographs to train AI models. Cash awards are paid within 30 calendar days of the announcement of results; no results date is published. — Deadline: January 6, 2027. Fee: €20 (1–4 photographs). Prize: €2,100 in cash awards + publication in a printed photobook and digital catalogue.

item.title: Shoot The Frame 2026 Annual Portrait Awards
item.description: The second edition of Shoot The Frame's Annual Portrait Award, from a platform that has run portrait, landscape and wildlife awards since 2012 and replaced its monthly contests with a single annual in 2025. Entries opened 1 November 2026 and close 31 December at 11:59pm US Pacific; the organiser publishes a two-day extension in its own timeline, to 2 January 2027 at 11:59pm Pacific. Two categories: One Frame, for single portraits each judged on its own merit, and Photo Essay, a curated series of up to fifteen portraits judged as one unified entry. One Frame is priced as packs — 1 photo $17, 3 for $27, 7 for $37 — and the Photo Essay is $49 for up to fifteen images; there is no cap on how many entries one photographer may submit. Prizes total US$4,000 in cash across six places: each category awards a winner US$1,000 and two finalists US$500 each. Both winners also receive a ViewSonic ColorPro monitor, and the Photo Essay winner a lifetime Format portfolio website. Every winner, finalist and honourable mention is published in the 2026 Annual Book, a softcover A4 volume printed in March 2027. Judging takes place in January 2027 and runs anonymously — the judges are named publicly but photographers are not identified to them — with winners and finalists announced in February. The 2026 panel is Tristan Hewat (founder), Tomasz Trzebiatowski (founder and editor-in-chief of FRAMES magazine), photographer and graphic designer Ian Pettigrew, and brand representatives from the two prize partners, ViewSonic and Format. Entry is open globally to amateurs and professionals of any age, with parental permission required under 18. Files are JPG, 2MB–10MB, sRGB, minimum 2000 pixels on the shortest edge. Photographers retain copyright and submitted images are used only to promote the awards, always with credit. AI-generated images are not allowed, nor are composite images or major digital manipulations; general editing and post-processing are permitted. Past placed photographers include Javier Arcenillas and Trevor Cole. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: $17–$49. Prize: US$4,000 in cash across 2 categories + ViewSonic monitor + publication in the 2026 Annual Book.

item.title: World Food Photography Awards 2027
item.description: The 2027 edition of the long-running international food photography competition run by Food Photographer of the Year Ltd, with entries open since 8 September 2026 and closing 7 February 2027. Twenty-seven categories cover the genre broadly — Food at the Table, Food for Sale, Food for Celebration, UNIDO Future of Food, A Feast of Flowers (a one-year-only category marking the 2027 Awards coinciding with the RHS Chelsea Flower Show), the Award for Innovation, the Newcomer Prize for first-time entrants, World Food Programme Food for Life, London Museum London Tastes, the Claire Aho Award for Women Photographers and a dedicated Louis Jadot Wine Photographer of the Year, plus On The Phone for smartphone work. The overall winner takes £5,000 and a trophy; all category winners receive a trophy and the opportunity to have their work displayed at the Mall Galleries, London in a free-to-enter public exhibition. Category finalists are invited to the VIP Awards Evening Reception at the Mall Galleries (travel and accommodation not included); the published exhibition offer is to winners rather than to all finalists. The Award for Innovation winner, supported by the Hugo Burge Foundation, gets a four-week residency in Scotland from 23 August to 19 September 2027 plus a £1,400 stipend; the Louis Jadot category winner takes £1,000. Standard entry is £35 per adult entrant covering up to six images, with further images at £7 each and no cap on the number submitted; the Food Stylist category is £35 per portfolio of five, and single entries to On The Phone are £7 (£2 of each going to Action Against Hunger). Three categories are free to enter, each capped at five entries: the Jamie Oliver Youth Prize for under-18s; the RPS Student Food Photographer of the Year, open to anyone currently attending — or within the previous twelve months having completed — a photography course at a recognised college or university, whose winner and two runners-up receive RPS membership, with the winner published by the RPS Journal and given two one-to-one mentoring sessions with a senior agent at At Collective; and UK for UNHCR Food as Home, open only to entrants with a refugee background or experience of forced displacement. Annual membership at £50 includes six free entries. The 2027 panel is chaired by the food photographer David Loftus and runs past fifty names across photography, publishing and food, among them Jamie Oliver, Deborah Willis (Chair of Photography, Tisch School of the Arts, NYU), Robin Hammond, Fiona Shields (Head of Photography, Guardian News & Media), Simon Hill (President, The Royal Photographic Society), Michael Pritchard (author of British Photographic History) and Karin van Gilst (Director, Foam Photography Museum). Shortlisted entrants are notified by the end of February 2027, judging takes place in March and the winners are announced on 18 May 2027. Generative AI is barred outright: it "must not be used to create, replace, extend or materially reconstruct any visual element of the entered image", entrants must retain original capture files, and breach risks disqualification and permanent exclusion; non-generative masking and retouching that introduces no invented food, props, surfaces, steam, garnishes, textures or backgrounds is allowed. Sponsors and partners include the World Food Programme, UK for UNHCR, UNIDO and Action Against Hunger. — Deadline: February 7, 2027. Fee: £35 (up to 6 entries) + £7 per extra; youth, student and UNHCR categories free. Prize: £5,000 + trophy and Mall Galleries London exhibition + 4-week residency in Scotland.

item.title: Your Photography Could Take Flight at Treasure Coast Airport · St. Lucie Cultural Alliance
item.description: A free, single-image public art call from the St. Lucie Cultural Alliance, a St. Lucie County arts organisation on Florida's Treasure Coast that is sponsored in part by the State of Florida's Division of Cultural Affairs, publishes Art St. Lucie Magazine, runs the Downtown Fort Pierce Art Walk and administers the county's Art in Public Places programme. One photograph will be reproduced as a professionally installed wrap on a Fort Pierce Utilities Authority utility box at Treasure Coast Airport in Fort Pierce - in the call's own words, ‘turning everyday infrastructure into a vibrant piece of public art’ - in a spot residents and travellers pass daily; neither surface says how long the wrap stays in place. The theme is open: aviation-themed work — airplanes, flight, aviation history, the spirit of travel — is encouraged as a natural fit for the location but is explicitly not required, and the call asks equally for landscapes, wildlife and anything that captures the beauty, energy or character of the Treasure Coast. Who can apply is stated plainly as photographers of all experience levels, with no residency or age bar on either surface, though the invitation is addressed to Treasure Coast photographers and the Cultural Alliance notes that its own members have preference in selection. There is no entry fee. Submission is one Cognito form per image, so a photographer entering more than one picture fills the form again; the form asks for the title, a description of the work, an uploaded image, and confirmation that you can supply a high-resolution file, since the printed wrap covers a box 58 inches tall and 56 inches wide with a 39-inch back. Two conditions are worth reading before you enter: the Cultural Alliance reserves the right to use digital images of accepted and exhibited artwork for its own promotion and publicity, and it states that while it will do its utmost to protect work in its possession it is not responsible for damage or loss. No artist fee, cash award or print stipend is named on the call page or the form — the opportunity on offer is the installation itself. No jurors or selection panel are named, and no notification date is published. — Deadline: November 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Public art exhibition at Treasure Coast Airport.

item.title: Between Seasons: Black & White Photography from City to Sea · Photo Art Pavilion
item.description: An annual juried, in-person black-and-white photography exhibition at the Southampton Cultural Center on the eastern end of Long Island, run by Photo Art Pavilion — the US art-photography marketplace and community founded by Joanne Henig and Jessica Lempin, who also founded Long Island Photo Gallery. Exactly 40 photographs are selected from the entries in a blind jury, with Henig and Lempin jurying and no artist names visible to them; selection runs on centre of interest, composition, focus and exposure, story, lighting, creativity and uniqueness rather than on one house style. All styles are welcome and the call is explicit that it does not care what the picture was made with — DSLR, point-and-shoot, smartphone or film — only that the work is black and white, the photographer's own and in keeping with the city-to-sea theme. The cash awards are $150 for first place, $125 for second, $100 for third and $35 for each honourable mention, announced live at the artists' reception rather than in advance, and the selected 40 are also published in an online gallery kept on PhotoArtPavilion.com in perpetuity. Entry is $37 for the first five images and $3 for each image after that, up to ten, with one submission per photographer; files are JPEGs at 72 dpi with the longest edge at least 1200 pixels, under 5 MB, free of watermarks or branding, and only the title is needed at upload. Note before you enter that this is a physical show on Long Island: work is delivered or installed on 1 March 2027, the exhibition runs 2–27 March, and every exhibiting artist is expected to attend the reception and awards in person on 27 March at noon Eastern, with pickup at 2:30 the same day. Southampton Cultural Center takes a 25% commission on any sale made during the show, and Photo Art Pavilion passes purchase enquiries straight to the artist on the artist's own terms. Open to photographers 18 and over, internationally, and notifications go out by the end of 15 January 2027. — Deadline: January 11, 2027. Fee: $37 for up to 5 images ($3 per additional image). Prize: $150 + $125 + $100 + Exhibition.

item.title: Résidence Incertitude 2027 · Freelens / IRIT
item.description: Freelens — the French photographers' association recognised as being of public utility — and IRIT, the CNRS computer-science research institute in Toulouse, run this annual photographic residency on the theme of uncertainty in science. It is conceived and directed by Cédric Févotte, CNRS research director at IRIT, with artistic direction by Céline Pévrier of sun/sun éditions. One photographer is invited to build a body of work across four to six weeks at IRIT, taken in one to three stays in the first half of 2027, with weekly check-ins and introductions to researchers whose expertise fits the project; applicants are asked not to approach IRIT scientists before applying. The laureate receives €6,000 inclusive of charges and VAT (of which €1,000 is the rights assignment for the presentation, exhibition and book), paid 40% on signature, 30% after the work with the publisher and 30% after the work with the exhibition venue, plus up to €3,000 for travel, accommodation in Toulouse and technical costs. On top of that sit a dedicated envelope for sun/sun éditions to publish a book of the project and a production budget for the resulting exhibition at Galerie Le Château d'Eau, the photography venue in Toulouse, alongside a public presentation at IRIT. The call is open to professional photographers — photographic authors or visual artists using the medium — French and international, who are fluent in French; the residency is open to pluridisciplinary projects that weave writing, sound or other modes into the photography. Applying is free but the règlement requires every applicant to join Freelens for €15 by card or PayPal, a membership that also covers every other Freelens event, grant and prize. The dossier is a single PDF of at most 20 pages and 10 MB: an intent note of up to five pages, a portfolio of up to fifteen, the proposed residency calendar, a one-page CV, a short bio and the completed application form, filed through the Google form by midnight on 30 November 2026. A pre-jury of Freelens board members and the residency's direction shortlists five candidates for a video interview before the final jury, which the règlement fixes at five seats — Févotte, Pévrier, Freelens president Sophie Knittel, one figure from the photography sector and one from scientific research. Interviews are scheduled for 17 December, subject to change, with the result announced "le 23 décembre 2027 au plus tard" as the page prints it. The 2026 laureate was Éléa-Jeanne Schmitter, and the residency carries the French Ministry of Culture's Bicentenaire de la Photographie label through 30 September 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: €15 Freelens membership (application itself free). Prize: €6,000 + 4–6 week residency + €3,000 expenses + Book publication + Exhibition.

item.title: The Photography Foundation Awards 2026
item.description: The Photography Foundation is the UK's largest photography-specific charity, and its annual awards are run as a fundraising project for that charity's work with emerging creatives. Every entrant gets one free image entry; each additional image is £8 and those fees are treated as donations. There are seven categories — Black and White (sponsored by Black+White Photography Magazine), Landscapes, urban and natural (Manfrotto), Music, Portraits & People (Capture One), Social Documentary (LIMI London), Street Photography and Wedding Photography — and entrants may submit as many images in as many categories as they wish. One overall winner receives £2,000 from Leica towards a new or ongoing photographic project. The winner and runner-up of the Black and White category are published in Black+White Photography Magazine; the Portraits & People winner gets a year of Capture One and a one-day pass to shoot at the Foundation's studio; the Landscapes winner receives a Manfrotto ONE Photo Alu tripod with XPRO ball head. Winners, runners-up and highly commended entrants are all exhibited at the annual Awards Exhibition, hosted by Leica London in 2025 and 2026 and by The Photobook Cafe before that. Judging is strictly anonymous — entrant details are stripped from the images and the eighteen judges vote independently of one another. The awards are explicitly open to amateurs as well as professionals, with entries accepted from all countries, and images must have been taken during 2026. The entry form does not sell single extra images: its dropdown offers one free entry, a 3-image pack at £16, 5 images at £32 or 10 at £72 — exactly £8 for every image past the free one, though the smallest paid outlay is £16 — alongside an optional £5–£100 donation that is not required to enter. The clause that bars AI also bars composites: entries must be authentic camera works, and "composite images, digital artwork, or images that incorporate elements not captured by the photographer through a camera lens are not eligible", with standard post-production allowed and the original RAW file open to request. An image that has already won the title of Overall Winner of another photographic competition cannot be entered, and files are JPEG or TIFF between 800KB and 5MB. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free for one image (£8 per additional image). Prize: £2,000 + magazine publication + exhibition.

item.title: Palermo Takeover 2027
item.description: Palermo Galerie is handing over its programme. From June to December 2027 the Stuttgart project space is opening its rooms to artists, collectives and curatorial teams and inviting independent proposals for exhibitions, performances, screenings, discussions and other experimental formats — “Your programme. Your ideas.” The space itself is the story: Palermo occupies the vacant former Schwabenbräu-Passage in Stuttgart-Bad Cannstatt, repurposed as a temporary gallery and project room for contemporary art until the owner modernises or demolishes the site, and it is run by Kunstverein Dialekt e.V., which has been supported by the City of Stuttgart's Kulturamt since 2005, with the gallery project additionally backed by the city's Liegenschaftsamt and Wirtschaftsförderung, the Bad Cannstatt district council, Dinkelacker Schwabenbräu, Werkstatthaus and Stuttgarter Jugendhaus gGmbH. The association states its position plainly: exhibitions are developed through cooperative and solidaristic processes, the focus is not the economic valorisation of artistic practice but the recognition of its intrinsic value and social dimension, and artists are treated not as entrepreneurial agents producing for a market segment but as producers of work that exists independently of exchange-value logic. It also writes the possibility of failure into its ethos as a productive force that enables experimentation. Be clear about what is and is not on offer, because the call is. What you get: rent-free space, existing technical equipment by arrangement and subject to availability, and 70% of food and drink revenue for your team with 30% going to the association. A total of €5,000 in funding has been applied for — and the call states that support will only be available if that funding is approved, so it cannot be counted on. What you carry: financing, organisation, publicity and any additional event permits required. This is a venue and a platform rather than a funded commission, which makes it a fit for a photographer or collective that already has a show in mind and wants a real room and an engaged audience rather than a prize. Applications run from 1 November 2026 to 15 January 2027 and consist of your concept, team information, a preliminary programme schedule, a funding strategy and work samples or links, sent by email. The call is published in German and English and sets no restriction on where applicants are based. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + revenue share.

item.title: PhotoForum Open Call 2026 — Photobooks and Online Exhibitions
item.description: PhotoForum Inc. — which has been publishing books and magazines since Photo-Forum magazine launched in 1974 and is funded primarily by its members — opens one call covering two strands of its 2027 programme, with a single email submission for both. The first is its print publishing programme: PhotoForum produces two publications a year and is looking for engaging recent photographic projects to be developed as its upcoming photobooks. The terms are stated plainly and are worth reading in full before applying. Each publication is issued as a limited edition with the majority sent to subscribed members; all publishing costs are covered by PhotoForum; copyright of the images remains with the artist; and the artists will not receive any payment but will receive five copies of the book. For a photographer with a resolved body of work and no publisher, a fully funded limited-edition photobook that costs nothing to enter is a substantial offer — but it is a publication, not a fee. The second strand is a series of online exhibitions planned for 2027, showcasing a wide selection of photographic work alongside newly commissioned writing, and these are open to individual photographers as well as partnerships, collaborations and collectives. Here there is money: selected photographers receive a modest fee for online publication, and publication will likely fall between March and November 2027. PhotoForum frames the commissioned writing as essential — it sees the involvement of writers as the way to create discourse around photographic artworks and widen the audience for both photography and the writing about it, which is also why its online exhibitions sit alongside a long-running essays and reviews programme rather than standing alone. Submissions for either strand are a PDF accompanied by a short artist statement of about 200 words and a bio. Decisions are made by PhotoForum's Publications and Online Subcommittees against three published criteria: do we love the work; is the proposed project cohesive and relatively resolved in its scope; and is the project consistent with the organisation's vision of continuing a strong legacy of significant photographic publications in Aotearoa New Zealand. The one hard gate is geography — submissions are welcomed from photographers based in Aotearoa New Zealand. The deadline is 5 pm on 23 November 2026. — Deadline: November 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + payment.

item.title: The Eyes are Bigger Than the Stomach: Food and Contemporary Art · Indy Art Center
item.description: A national juried exhibition at the Indy Art Center built on a subject the organiser calls universal: “There are few things so universal and central to the human experience as food. It has shaped cultures, customs, geography, politics and much more across centuries.” The question put to artists is how we reflect on food through contemporary art in 2026 — including the contemporary edges of it, which the call names explicitly: food scarcity, factory farming, climate change. The brief is deliberately open on medium: this is a call “open to any artist working within the theme or concept of food with no specified medium required”, and the Art Center states that all artworks which connect to food in some way, through media, concept or theme, will be considered, with jurors approaching the theme under an encompassing definition covering both traditional techniques and contemporary methods of making. For a photographer that is a wide door — documentary work on agriculture and the food supply, still life, studio and alternative-process work all sit inside it — and the eligibility clause confirms it: entries are open to artists 18 or older residing in the United States, working in any media, with work made within the last two years that has not been shown at the Art Center before. Entry is two works for $35 with $5 for each additional piece up to a maximum of fifteen, and awards are cash: $300 Best in Show, $150 Best in 2D, $150 Best in 3D and two honourable mentions of $100 each. The exhibition is a long one — it opens 5 April 2027 and closes 13 June, with the reception on 16 April, 5 to 8 pm — and it runs in six galleries at an institution that mounts more than a dozen contemporary art exhibitions a year. Practical terms worth knowing before applying: all work may be offered for sale and the Art Center retains a 35% commission on sales; the artist pays shipping, insurance in transit and return shipping, and work must arrive in a reusable container by 21 March 2027 (hand delivery opens 20 February); work must not exceed 250 pounds or ten feet in any direction; and installation artists are asked to make contact before applying. The deadline is 17 February 2027 with notifications by end of day on the 19th. — Deadline: February 17, 2027. Fee: $35 (two works) + $5 per additional work. Prize: $300 + $150 ×2 + $100 ×2 + Exhibition.

item.title: Solo Exhibition December 2026 · All About Photo
item.description: All About Photo runs a Solo Exhibition every month, and December 2026 is the next open slot. The selected photographer gets the whole month — 1 to 31 December 2026 — across the site's home page, competition gallery and photography exhibition directory, plus an exclusive interview, a dedicated portfolio page holding 20 images in the Photographers Directory, and a permanent place in the showroom archive after the month ends. The organiser also commits to specific press: a special-edition newsletter announcing the exhibition, promotion across its Instagram, Facebook and Twitter accounts, and guaranteed publication on Bored Panda, Visura and Photophiles Magazine, with past winners having been picked up by The Times UK, National Geographic España, The Eye of Photography and Digital Camera World. Sales during the exhibition are commission-free — the photographer keeps the full price. The juror for this cycle is Olga Karlovac, a self-taught photographer based in Zagreb whose trilogy “before winter”, “the disarray” and “escape” sold out its first edition and whose work has run in Black+White Photography and the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung. The theme is open and every genre is invited — photojournalism, street, fine art, landscape, portraiture — from professionals and enthusiasts alike, anywhere in the world. What matters is cohesion: the entry is 6 to 14 images for a flat $45, and the organiser is explicit that only cohesive projects or portfolios will be published as a Solo Exhibition, so a set of unrelated strong frames is the wrong submission here. Two practical notes. This is an online-only exhibition — there is no physical venue and no cash prize; what is awarded is a month of placement, an interview and the press package above, so judge the $45 against visibility rather than against an award. And entry runs through an account on All About Photo's own site: the “Enter Competition” button redirects to the site's sign-in and back to this page, so there is no separate submission portal to bookmark. The deadline is Tuesday 17 November 2026, two weeks before the exhibition opens. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: PhotoSpiva 2027 · Spiva Center for the Arts
item.description: PhotoSpiva is the longest-running photographic competition of its kind in the United States — Spiva Center for the Arts in Joplin, Missouri has run it every year since 1977, and the 2027 edition follows the 50th. The founders' brief still governs it: “present an exhibition of excellence in photography, celebrating the scope and vigorous activity of today's contemporary photographers”, and co-founder Jim Mueller's note that “we have intentionally avoided any categorization of either photographers or their work” is why there is still no theme and no category. Any photographic process qualifies — traditional, digital or photo-based mixed media — provided the work is two-dimensional, original, and has never been exhibited at Spiva before; three-dimensional work is not eligible. Entry is open to any amateur or professional photographer in the United States or its territories, with no age floor and no career-stage bar. Selected work hangs 20 March – 29 May 2027 in Spiva's galleries in the Harry M. Cornell Arts & Entertainment Complex, with the opening reception and awards on Friday 19 March 2027, 5:30–7:30 pm. The award ladder is cash and substantial for a $40 entry: $1,000 first, $750 second, $500 third, three $150 Merit Awards and three $100 Honorable Mentions — $3,000 in all. A new juror is invited each year from among, in the organiser's words, the nation's most respected photographers and curators; the 2027 jurors are Louviere+Vanessa, the collaborative duo whose work crosses photography, film, painting and printmaking, named on the call's own CaFE record — the organiser's own page has not caught up and still carries the 2026 juror, Dan Winters. Know the fee structure before you start: the $40 buys exactly five images and you must enter five, no fewer — the prospectus explicitly allows entering the same photograph five times if you do not have five — and each image beyond the fifth is $10. All images must go in one application; files are JPEG in RGB, with roughly 1600 pixels on the long edge given as a guideline rather than a rule. Acceptance or declination is sent by email by 27 January 2027. Two costs land only if you are selected. Accepted work must be printed, mounted on a rigid backing and matted — and may not be framed; Spiva partners with a local print house that offers accepted artists discounted printing and matting, though you may prepare your own to its specifications. Shipping and insurance both ways are the artist's responsibility, and the Center's “all risk” policy covers only theft and fire. Sale is optional, and the split on anything sold is 60% to the artist. Entering grants Spiva the right to reproduce an entry for publicity tied to this or future exhibitions. Two things to check before you click through. The entry window opens on 6 November 2026 at midnight Central, so the CaFE record carries no apply button until then — at the time of listing its page showed the prospectus but not the “Apply on CaFE” route a live sibling record carries. And the organiser's own page contradicts itself: its “How to Participate” block is stale and still prints the 2026 cycle's “Begin entering on November 7, 2025” and “Deadline is Jan 5, 2026”, while its “terms and conditions” link opens the 2026 prospectus. The binding window is the one in the “PhotoSpiva 2027 Key Dates” block and in the 2027 prospectus: 6 November 2026 to 4 January 2027 at 11:59 pm Central. The competition is presented by Freeman Health System with support from the Missouri Arts Council. — Deadline: January 4, 2027. Fee: $40 (5 images) + $10 each additional. Prize: $1,000 + $750 + $500 + 3×$150 + 3×$100 + Exhibition.

item.title: New Year Commission 2027 · Photoworks
item.description: Photoworks, a registered charity that describes itself as the only organisation with a national remit for photography in England, is commissioning one photographer or lens-based artist to make a single new image marking the start of 2027. The organisation has no physical venue — the Brighton address on this listing is its postal address, and the commission runs entirely online. The brief is deliberately loose and playful: a non-conventional image that indicates the beginning of a new year, with room to experiment rather than illustrate. The commission pays a £500 fee and comes with an Instagram takeover of the Photoworks account in January 2027. The finished image travels further than most single-image commissions: Photoworks shares it across its social platforms, sends it to a mailing list that it describes as including curators, editors, artists and industry professionals, and prints it as a postcard that ships with every Photoworks shop order through 2027. Entry is free and no images are uploaded — the form carries no file field at all — but the application is more than a link: it asks for your name and email, a portfolio link (website or Instagram), and a written answer to “How would you approach creating an image for this commission?”. Everything after that, from location and age range to ethnicity, gender and caring responsibilities, is optional equal-opportunities monitoring, and applying adds you to the Photoworks mailing list. The call is explicitly international: the organisation says it looks forward to hearing from applicants wherever they are in the world, the form's location question offers “Outside the UK, please state country”, and the organiser's standing page for this commission says it goes to an artist at any stage in their career. Three things to know before applying. No selection panel is named and no notification date is published, so there is no stated timetable between the 5 December deadline and the January takeover. The deadline is printed as “Deadline 5 December.” with no time of day, and this organiser does publish one when it has one — its previous Photography+ open call closed at 9:00 am GMT — so treat 5 December as the last safe day rather than a full one. And note the route: the page's web address still carries last year's slug while the page itself is headed New Year Commission 2027, and the only 2026 inside the call block is the credit line on Ning Cheng's previous commission. — Deadline: December 5, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £500 + Publication.

item.title: The Meridian Award — Cycle III
item.description: An independent international award granting a $2,000 fully unrestricted cash prize to one contemporary artist working in any medium, with $200 to each of two finalists. Founded in New York City, it is open to all artists aged 18 and over worldwide with no restriction on nationality, location, education or professional status, and there is no theme — portfolios are judged on artistic merit, clarity of vision, coherence of the work presented and the strength of a distinct artistic perspective. Photography is named in the award's own discipline list alongside painting, drawing, digital art, sculpture, print-based media, textile-based media, performance, sound art, video art and interdisciplinary practice; short and feature-length films are the only stated exclusion. Winner and both finalists are invited to an individual interview published on the award's website and Instagram. Apply through the award's own form with a name, a biography (150 words), an artist statement (250 words), a work description and up to five files, images and video links combined, each image under 2MB and named for its artwork; a separate portfolio PDF is not required. The fee is $30, non-refundable, and no fee waivers are offered. Two things to weigh. The jurors are described as invited contemporary-art professionals but are not publicly named, which the organiser states is deliberate. And this third cycle is twice as rich as the last — Cycle II paid $1,000 at a $25 fee — while the award's own About page still reads "The second cycle of The Meridian Award is now officially open for applications"; it is the FAQ that labels the January 15, 2027 deadline as Cycle III. The payout record is real: the inaugural 2026 cycle went to Brooklyn sculptor Wen Liu, a 2026 AIM Fellow at the Bronx Museum with fellowships from Yaddo, MacDowell and Bogliasco, with painter Matt Bollinger and interdisciplinary artist Andrius Alvarez-Backus as finalists. That is also the only result the award has published so far; the cycle that closed on October 18, 2026 has not been announced. Artists keep full copyright; by applying they agree their materials may be used for the award's promotional and editorial posts. The winner is announced in February 2027. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $30. Prize: $2,000 + two $200 finalist awards.

item.title: Drone Photo Awards 2027 · Siena Awards
item.description: Siena Awards' aerial photography contest returns for 2027 with nine categories and a prize package that helps cover the stay in Italy. The rules open with the eligibility line — “Drone Photo Awards competition is open to professional and amateur photographers”. Seven single-shot categories are published (Wedding, Nature, People, Urban, Animals, Abstract and Sport), alongside a Videos category and a Series category, where “You may enter from 5 to 9 images” on “a set of images that are presented together on the same theme, edited in the same style, and with a common link.” Six of the single-shot briefs define the work as “captured from the sky” and Abstract as “Aerial photography”, though neither the Videos nor the Series brief states an aerial requirement of its own. Entry is free for one image; beyond that the rules' Entry Fees table reads “3 images (including the free one) € 30”, “Each additional image € 10”, and € 35 for a Series or a Videos entry, with “no refunds provided” once paid. The entrant “with the highest scoring image will be endowed the title of ‘Drone Photographer of the Year’” and there is also a winner in each category; the overall winner receives “€ 500,00 worth of photography equipment”, the “Pangea Prize” crystal trophy, and “a fixed fee of 400 euros to assist with accommodation expenses for two overnight stays in Siena during the Awards Ceremony weekend”, reimbursed after the winners are announced. Two conditions attach to the awards: the trophies and parchments “will only be given to winners attending the Awards Ceremony”, and equipment “not collected during the ceremony will be the responsibility of the winners”. Winners are honoured on stage at the ceremony in Siena, and “the winning images will be showcased in Siena at the ‘Above Us Only Sky’ exhibition during 2 months”, with advertising in the international press. Photographers keep their copyright — “Siena Awards recognizes you retain full ownership of the copyright in each photograph that you have submitted” — and grant only promotional use of entered images. AI is barred outright: the rules prohibit AI generation software “for the creation or enhancement of images”, including AI-generated elements added to camera-captured frames and generative fill used to extend an image beyond its original boundaries. No 2027 juror is named — entries are “reviewed and pre-screened by our editors and an international group of industry professionals”, then judged by “our international jury”, and the award's jury route serves only the roster of previous editions. Entries opened on 11 October 2026 and close on 1 June 2027. — Deadline: June 1, 2027. Fee: Free (1 image); €30/3, €10 each extra; €35 Series/Videos. Prize: €500 gear + €400 accommodation + exhibition.

item.title: Rooted + Rising · Pierro Gallery
item.description: A free, no-commission municipal gallery show for Black artists, with photography named in the gallery's own accepted media. The Pierro Gallery of South Orange describes Rooted + Rising as bringing “together local and regional Black artists whose work reflects the many ways history, culture, creativity, pride, resilience, and activism continue to shape contemporary expression. These artists carry stories and traditions forward while making something entirely their own, reminding us that culture is not static—it grows, changes, and finds new ways to speak.” Eligibility is stated in one line on the call: “Emerging and established local and regional artists are welcome to apply” — the gallery sets no county or state boundary anywhere on the call or in its guidelines, and its standing exhibitions policy reads that artists are “featured with special sensitivity to regional artists but without precluding consideration of work by any visual artist”, so the geography is a preference rather than a published bar. Up to three works may be submitted with title, medium, dimensions, year and price; a short artist statement and bio are asked for only from artists who are selected, who are also sent a Release of Liability form to sign. Images should be kept under 10 MB, and the gallery states it “cannot respond to inquiries or provide feedback on individual pieces” because of submission volume. Photography is explicitly welcome — the gallery's FAQ lists “paintings, sculptures, photography and mixed media” — and work needing glass or Plexiglass must meet standard framing guidelines (flat wood or metal, white, black or natural preferred, no more than 1″ wide from the front, no decorative frames unless part of the artwork), with unconventionally presented works on paper accepted if the presentation is professional. There is no submission fee: “We do not charge a submission fee. We believe in providing artists with an opportunity to showcase their work without financial barriers.” Sales are allowed and the gallery takes nothing from them — it “operates on a non-commission basis” and asks only for a voluntary donation. Founded in 1994 and named for the late artist and arts advocate Lennie Pierro, the gallery is run by South Orange's Department of Recreation and Cultural Affairs at the Baird Community Center. Artists are notified the week of 14 December 2026, drop-off is mid-January, and the exhibition runs 4 February to 4 April 2027. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: story · A Smith Gallery
item.description: A Smith Gallery's next juried online show takes narrative as its subject — "story: adventure, tale, narrative, myth, drama, fable, saga, fiction, novel, fantasy…." — and the gallery makes good on the theme itself: co-director Kevin Tully, writing as Frank Cincinnatus, "will write a short tale to go along with the Juror and Director Award images", and the prospectus prints a sample of his fiction in full. Tully is also the juror; he is a photographer, designer, writer and artist who "has curated and installed hundreds of exhibitions for the gallery" and has juried for All About Photo, Analogue Forever, Dodho Magazine, the International Photography Hall of Fame and Critical Mass. The call is open and unlimited: "The competition is open to all photographers both professional and amateur working in all photographic mediums and styles. International entries are welcomed", at $40 for the first five images and $5 for each additional one, with "no limit to the number of images you may submit"; work previously shown in an A Smith Gallery competition is not eligible. Jurying is blind, with images renamed and numbered. Up to 47 images are selected for an online exhibition that is permanently archived, featured image by image on the gallery's Facebook and Instagram, discussed in a recorded GalleryTalk, listed for sale in the gallery's online store and published in a purchasable exhibition catalogue; 27 of the 47 also go into "The 27", a hardbound fine art book. The Juror and Director Awards each bring "a online solo exhibition, 'The 27' exhibition book and feature story on the gallery blog", and the Visitors Award, decided by Instagram likes, pays $100. Photographers submitting 13 or more images get a free 30-minute review with the gallery directors; fewer than 13 costs $20 for the same. Photographers keep full rights, the gallery takes 30% of any sale, and a sold print may be shipped by the artist or printed by the gallery. The exhibition runs 8 January to 18 February 2027. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images + $5 each. Prize: $100 + Solo exhibition.

item.title: PhotoWings x Photoville Educator Exhibition Grant 2027
item.description: The tenth edition of a grant that puts school students’ photographs into a major public festival. Photoville, with PhotoWings, invites middle and high school educators to propose an exhibition of their students’ work for the 2027 Photoville Festival, which spreads across Brooklyn Bridge Park and all five boroughs. Six educators are selected, and each receives "Curatorial, design, printing, and logistical support from the Photoville team", "A public exhibition of their students’ work as part of the 2027 Photoville Festival" and "A $500 cash grant". READ BOTH OF PHOTOVILLE’S OWN PAGES, BECAUSE THEY STATE ELIGIBILITY DIFFERENTLY. The festival homepage gives only a school-level bar: "This program is ONLY open to Middle and High School Educators who work directly with students. School Administrators and Elementary and College programs will not be considered." The grant’s own info page — the route that homepage links as its "info page" — adds a condition the homepage never mentions, and softens the geography: "This grant is open to all middle and high school educators who have participated in a Photoville Education program in the past. Please note that New York City based schools will be given priority in the selection process." So New York is a stated priority rather than a bar, and the grant’s own published recipient list runs past the five boroughs: alongside schools in the Bronx, Park Slope and Staten Island it names the Issaquah High School Photo Club and the all-Tribal "Our Community Record Two Eagle River School, Confederated Salish & Kootenai Tribes". The prior-participation clause, though, is stated flatly, so an educator new to Photoville should ask before building a proposal. The grant builds on "9 years of collaboration with educators to develop lesson plans inspired by photography projects", and what it funds is the exhibition that comes out of teaching one: educators "implement a photo-based lesson from the Photoville Educator Resource library in their classroom and produce a culminating exhibition of student work". Photoville notes that "for the past 8 years we have seen a vastly dynamic array of students’ work". Proposals go through Photoville’s own submission form, which closes "January 4, 2027 at 11:59pm ET"; the festival’s separate artist call for proposals closes earlier, on 22 December 2026. Photoville Festival is supported in part by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council. — Deadline: January 4, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $500 + exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Call for Entries — Detroit · Subjectively Objective
item.description: The photobook publisher Subjectively Objective is opening "a new series of exhibitions at our soon to be expanded Detroit area gallery space" and taking submissions of up to ten images. There is no theme: "This is an open call with no specific theme, as this will allow us the greatest ability to create a variety of interesting exhibitions. Our primary focus is on contemporary landscape and documentary photography, but even if your work falls outside of that, please don't hold back from submitting." Work not placed in one of these shows is still considered for the publisher's other channels — "our Substack Features, Instagram Features, and Mini and Monthly Monograph Magazines" — and returning contributors are explicitly invited back. READ THE COST STRUCTURE BEFORE YOU APPLY: the $10 submission fee is only the entry, and "if selected, the artist will be responsible for an exhibition fee that covers the cost of producing their exhibition print(s), the opening, and promoting the physical exhibition." You pick the largest print size you want to be considered for — you remain eligible for smaller ones — and that choice sets the bill if you are taken: $30 per image for a small print (about 15x12 inches), $45 medium, $65 large (25x20), $90 XL (30x24), $150 XXL (40x32), $300 for a full eight-foot wall, $350–600 for a wall of larger prints, and $600+ for multiple walls, the last being "for those open to the possibility of participation in a small group show or even a solo exhibition". Printing is done in house by founder Noah Waldeck, who "will be using the same expert techniques he uses to make museum quality prints for his custom lab clients", and after the show he will send your print on if you cover shipping. The submission fee itself is waivable: "If you can't afford the submission fee, please contact me and we'll figure something out." Instructions arrive as a downloadable PDF once the fee is paid. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $10 + $30–$600+ exhibition fee if selected. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Photoville Festival 2027 — Call for Proposals
item.description: The 16th annual Photoville returns to New York for "three weeks of free public art, exhibitions, and community programming in Brooklyn Bridge Park and across all five boroughs", and the call is as wide as the festival: "We are looking for ALL types of photographic and lens-based work. We welcome everything from documentary and photojournalism, to fine art, sports, and conceptual work. Alternative processes such as photo collage, tintypes, and cyanotypes are all welcome too!" The festival wants "global narratives, local histories, studio portraiture, street photography, collaborative archives, community-driven projects, and interdisciplinary approaches" and work on "immigration, healthcare, education, racial inequality, climate change, social justice, incarceration, women's rights, youth and intergenerational stories, police reform, housing, joy". Because the shows stand in public parks, it asks you to "avoid images that may be shocking — particularly images of nudity, sexual intercourse, drug use, or violence". There are three applications — two for exhibitions (open-air structures sited across the five boroughs, and the festival's signature shipping containers in Brooklyn Bridge Park) and one for public programming, a talk, workshop or interactive experience; you may submit more than one proposal, and Photoville steers unsponsored artists to the open-air route because container slots are few and costly. The economics are the point: "Independent artists selected for the festival do not pay exhibition costs. Photoville covers all design, production and installation expenses to ensure equitable participation." For a selected artist or artist-led collective with no institutional support or sponsorship, Photoville states it will "cover the cost of printing, exhibition structures, installation, public liability insurance, publicity, and will pay a modest artist honorarium", the amount varying with the number of artists supported and the scope of the project. Artists, non-profits and commercial entities that DO arrive with sponsorship are asked for a contribution instead, assessed per proposal and quoted at $5,000–$40,000 for open-air and $12,000–$40,000 for a container.
